"""Polynomial-time reduction from Subset Sum to Partition.

Subset Sum instance: {"numbers": [a1, ...], "target": t}, numbers >= 0.
Partition instance:  {"numbers": [a1, ...]},          numbers >= 0.

Reduction
---------
Let S = sum(numbers).

* If t < 0 or t > S, the Subset Sum answer is "no" (all numbers are
  non-negative, so no sub-list can sum to a negative value or to more than
  the total).  Return the Partition instance {"numbers": [1]}, whose total
  is odd and which is therefore always "no".

* Otherwise t <= S, so b = S - 2t >= 0.  Return the Partition instance
  {"numbers": numbers + [b]}.  Its total is S + b = 2(S - t), so a valid
  partition splits it into two groups of sum S - t.

  Equivalence:
    (=>) If some sub-list X of numbers sums to t, then its complement
         numbers \ X sums to S - t, and X + [b] sums to
         t + (S - 2t) = S - t.  So the partition exists.
    (<=) If a sub-list Y of numbers + [b] sums to S - t, then either
         b in Y, in which case Y \ {b} is a sub-list of numbers summing to
         (S - t) - (S - 2t) = t; or b not in Y, in which case Y is a
         sub-list of numbers summing to S - t, so its complement in numbers
         sums to t.  Either way Subset Sum is "yes".

The reduction is polynomial: it only computes S and appends one number.
"""

from typing import Any
